Same extraction as v3 -- no re-extraction, this run is entirely schema/pipeline-code changes re-parsed over the existing raw JSON, so the gold-eval score is unchanged (expected: field-match scoring doesn't check date_undate or session completeness). Replaced is_dark (bool) with session_status enum (performed/no_performance) per user request ('dark cell' isn't an intuitive name), and added a third analysis-layer-only value, not_captured, in analysis.performance_session: for every Repertoire page, an expected date x theater grid (era/city-aware theater roster, docs/schema.md) is left-joined against what was actually captured, and any missing (date, theater) combination is inserted as a not_captured placeholder rather than silently absent -- 3771 gaps found (~13.7% of the full expected grid), unevenly distributed across seasons/pages, consistent with issue #1 being page-level non-determinism rather than a uniform rate. Building this surfaced two real, previously-undetected date-parsing bugs in schemas/dates.py (known_issues.md #14): abbreviated months (Февр., Апр., etc.) weren't matching at all (fixed date_undate fill rate 89.0%->99.8%), and season-spanning year ranges (1896-1897 гг.) always resolved to the first year even for Jan-Jul months, silently mis-dating those sessions by a full year (found via an obviously-wrong 365-day page span). Also found and normalized (analysis-layer theater_canonical, raw.theater untouched, known_issues.md #15): post-1898-99 pages consistently append театръ/театр to theater names where earlier pages don't, and Маріинскій is sometimes spelled Мариинскій (missing the pre-reform і, 116 occurrences across 4 seasons) -- both would silently break any exact-match join on theater identity, which is exactly how the completeness reconciliation initially (and wrongly) showed 100% gap rate for every 1898-99+ season before the fix. Three rarer field-boundary mixups involving theater documented but not fixed (known_issues.md #16): city-total summary rows, a table-header row captured as data, and one ballet title swapped into the theater field (2 rows). Net effect: this run doesn't change the accuracy score, but substantially improves the trustworthiness of anything built on session_status/date_undate/theater going forward, and gives a precise, page-level completeness signal to target a DashScope thinking-mode re-extraction experiment against, instead of re-running the whole corpus with it on.

Full corpus, all 7 sourced entity types (RepertoireTables, Administration, BalletArtists, Musicians, ProductionTeam, TheaterSchoolStaff, Graduates -- ProductionStats still not sourced), all 18 seasons, run locally end to end (render/extract/parse/quality/duckdb), processed one entity-type category at a time (render->extract->delete-images) because most source PDFs were iCloud "Optimize Mac Storage" placeholders and available local disk (~14-20GB) could not hold a full 300dpi render of the whole corpus at once. 1076/1076 pages extracted, 0 unresolved failures: 12 oversized 1896-97 Repertoire pages hit DashScope 20MB payload limit as PNG, same known issue as the July run, fixed by re-encoding those 12 pages to JPEG (~2MB each) and retrying. parse_and_validate.py found 2 new (not previously seen) roster validation gaps beyond known_issues.md #7: (1) NAME_IN_HEADING_RE did not match names with a leading noble title ("Графъ Бобринскій, ...") or a trailing rank suffix ("..., тит. сов.") -- regex broadened to handle both, keeping title text in family_name and rank text in heading_path rather than discarding it; (2) 7 entries across 2 pages (administration_1904-05_p002, productionteam_1892-93_p002) had heading_path set to a bare section heading ("Дежурные врачи", "Парикмахеры") with no name anywhere in the JSON -- confirmed against the scanned pages these are genuine model omissions, not a field-boundary issue, so no name was fabricated; _repair_roster now drops only that single unrecoverable entry (logged to validation_errors.csv as entry_dropped_no_name) instead of the previous behavior of failing pydantic validation for the WHOLE page. Quality flags mix matches the July run pattern (rank_class_left_in_heading_path fully recovered by build_duckdb.py analysis-layer regex, same as before). ~11.24M tokens billed total (incl. the 1896-97 JPEG retry batch). Scores close to the July v3/v4 run (82.6/96.3/86.7) -- small differences expected from VLM sampling non-determinism (known_issues.md #1), not a regression. Did not run entity-resolution/research-model/publishing stages this session.

CORRECTS the full_run_2026-08-15_qwen3-vl-plus_local row above, which was reported complete but was NOT: RepertoireTables only had 8/18 seasons (246/519 pages) processed at that time. Root cause: earlier in this session, before understanding the iCloud "Optimize Mac Storage" eviction behavior, a partial prior render (13/18 season PNGs, from a run that later crashed) was manually migrated into outputs/full_run/images to avoid re-work. By the time the real Repertoire batch ran, most of those PDFs had been silently re-evicted to iCloud-only placeholders again -- and render_pages.py's discover_pdfs uses folder.glob("*.pdf"), which does not match evicted/placeholder files at all (they appear under a different, hidden .xxx.pdf.icloud name), so those PDFs were silently skipped rather than erroring -- only 8 of 18 got into that manifest, with no crash or error to signal the gap. Existing pre-rendered PNGs for the skipped seasons sat unused in images/, uncounted, surviving the post-extraction cleanup because cleanup only deletes page_ids present in the run manifest. Caught by manually cross-checking the actual PDF/page counts the pipeline log reported per category against the true on-disk file counts established at the start of the session -- RepertoireTables was the only category where a mismatch showed up (8 PDFs found vs 18 expected); all 6 Spiski_* categories matched their true counts exactly. Fixed by re-rendering (all 18 PDFs were, by then, naturally re-materialized) and extracting the missing 273 pages -- which surfaced the SAME oversized-PNG/20MB DashScope limit issue (known_issues.md #19 / the original July run) on three more early-season files (1890-91, 1891-92, 1897-98, 24 pages), fixed the same way (JPEG re-encode at ~1.5-1.8MB/page). That JPEG retry initially still failed for those same 24 pages for a distinct second reason: the ORIGINAL oversized PNGs for those 3 seasons were themselves leftovers from the same stale migration and had never been deleted, and run_pilot.py checks for a .png before falling back to .jpg -- so it kept picking the old oversized PNG over the new correctly-sized JPEG until those stale PNGs were explicitly deleted. Final state after all fixes: 1349/1349 pages extracted, 0 unresolved failures, 0 page-level parse failures (same 2 pre-existing entry-level drops as before, see known_issues.md #19). 13,908,280 tokens billed in total across every invocation this session (initial batches + all retries). Scores now closely track the July v3/v4 baseline (82.6/96.3/86.7 vs this run's 80.9/96.2/86.1) as expected from VLM sampling non-determinism, not the gap seen in the mistaken interim row. Lesson for next time: after any run that involves reusing pre-rendered images from an earlier partial/crashed attempt, verify the pipeline's own reported N-PDFs-found count against the true on-disk file count for every category, not just spot-check the ones that seem risky. ADDENDUM (same run, added after further inspection): the 80.9%/86.1% headline match rates above understate true accuracy -- roughly half of all 226 field mismatches in this run's eval_report.txt turned out to be a single artifact, not real errors: eval_against_gold.py compares gold and predicted roster rows by raw list position (zip()), so on 2 of the 12 gold pages where the model's entry list had a couple of extra real people the gold excerpt had skipped, every row after that point compared against the wrong person even though the underlying data was correct once realigned (hand-verified: shifting one page's predicted list by +3 rows made all 14 gold rows match exactly, byte for byte). After removing that cascade plus 2 other already-tracked non-error patterns (issue #2/#3-style boundary and punctuation differences), the rate of genuinely isolated, real content errors was 31/1627 fields = ~1.9%, not ~14%. See known_issues.md #21 and docs/eval/README.md for the full methodology caveat -- this also means eval_against_gold.py's reported percentage should not be quoted at face value for any run until that script's row-matching is fixed to align by identity instead of position.
